content.title: Bitter cold, snow forecast for eastern US over next several days
content.text: Two systems are moving through the eastern U.S. over the next few days.ByMELISSA GRIFFIN and MAX GOLEMBOFebruary 1, 2018, 2:40 PM— -- The Midwest was hit with a blast of snow today and that cold front continues to move east, bringing with it rain, snow and cold temperatures.A pedestrian crosses the street during a snow storm in Boston, Mass., on Jan. 30, 2018.Brian Snyder/ReutersWinter weather advisories are in effect for eastern Kentucky, Tennessee and parts of West Virginia, where 1 to 3 inches of snow is expected.On Thursday a cold front is expected to move east with rain, snow, and cold temperatures behind it.Rain is expected overnight from Washington, D.C., to Boston, and the precipitation will turn to snow in the early morning hours.Forecasts show overnight the precipitation starting off as rain from Washington, D.C. to Boston before turning to snow in the early morning hours.By 6 a.m. Friday the snow will have already moved through D.C. to New York City with some snow lingering in Boston and coastal areas including the New Jersey shore, Long Island and Southeast New England.By 6 a.m. on Friday, the snow has already moved through D.C. to New York with some snow lingering in Boston and coastal areas and Southeast New England.Snow accumulation is expected to be fairly minor in those areas because the front will move through quickly. But the changeover from rain to snow will surely bring some slick spots for the Friday morning commute.Arctic blastA fresh arctic blast will stretch from the Upper Midwest to the Northeast on Friday.Popular ReadsOn Friday morning wind chills will fall to negative 24 degrees in Minneapolis, minus 4 degrees in Buffalo, minus 17 degrees in Green Bay, minus 2 degrees in Pittsburgh and even 3 degrees in Charleston.Friday morning wind chills are 10 to 30 degrees below zero for parts of the Upper Midwest.Friday night wind chills are expected to reach 8 degrees in Philadelphia, 5 degrees in New York, 1 degree in Boston and negative 6 degrees in Syracuse.A cold and blustery Friday is on tap for the Northeast; wind chills will be in the single digits from Philadelphia to Boston through Saturday morningAmerican Airlines passenger planes prepare for takeoff at Boston Logan International Airport in Boston, Mass., on Jan 30, 2018.CJ GuntherEPA via ShutterstockSuper Bowl forecastMore snow and rain are coming as well as another arctic blast Saturday into Sunday.Minneapolis will see some snow on Saturday. Wind chills are expected to be at least negative 20 degrees for Super Bowl Sunday.Sponsored Content by Taboola
